newsitem.title: USA: SEC official warns against fund performance misuse.
newsitem.headline: SEC official warns against fund performance misuse.

text.p: An official at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission Friday warned a mutual fund industry group against providing customers with misleading information about prior fund performance.
"Industry participants would be ill-advised to assume anything goes when it comes to presentations of prior performance," said Barry Barbash, head of the agency's Division of Investment Management.
He was speaking at the Investment Company Institute's annual conference.
Barbash told reporters that the SEC has not yet decided what approach it will take to help curtail potential misrepresentations to customers.
"First we want to get more information," he said, adding that the agency plans to talk to mutual fund industry representatives.

Separately, Barbash said federal securities and pension laws will have to be updated to do away with outdated and duplicative regulations. He said problems in this area will be compounded by 2011 when baby boomers are withdrawing retirement savings and investments.
"The year 2000 problem will seem small indeed by the time we reach 2011," Barbash said.
He warned that if federal regulators do not step up to the plate and modernize federal rules governing the securities and pension plan investments, Congress will take the matter into its hands.
"If the regulators fail to meet this challenge, Congress will step in," Barbash cautioned.
His comments come as lawmakers threatened to overturn rules the agency adopted earlier this year requiring companies to disclose potential fluctuations in the value of their derivatives holdings.
